passages.text: Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off every encumbrance and the sin that so easily entangles, and let us run with endurance the race set out for us.
passages.sermon:
We are surrounded by a great cloud of witnesses.
These witnesses are people who lived by faith.
Let us throw off every weight that holds us back.
Let us also throw off the sin that easily entangles us.
Let us run the race set before us.
Let us run with endurance.
passages.original: Τοιγαροῦν καὶ ἡμεῖς τοσοῦτον ἔχοντες περικείμενον ἡμῖν νέφος μαρτύρων ὄγκον ἀποθέμενοι πάντα καὶ τὴν εὐπερίστατον ἁμαρτίαν δι’ ὑπομονῆς τρέχωμεν τὸν προκείμενον ἡμῖν ἀγῶνα

passages.text: Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy set before Him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the author of our faith.
Jesus is the perfecter of our faith.
Let us look to Jesus.
God set a great joy before Jesus.
Jesus endured the cross for this joy.
Jesus despised the shame of the cross.
God seated Jesus at His right hand.
God’s throne is in heaven.
Jesus now sits at the right hand of God’s throne.
passages.original: ἀφορῶντες εἰς τὸν τῆς πίστεως ἀρχηγὸν καὶ τελειωτὴν Ἰησοῦν ὃς ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης αὐτῷ χαρᾶς ὑπέμεινεν σταυρὸν αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας ἐν δεξιᾷ τε τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ Θεοῦ κεκάθικεν

passages.text: Consider Him who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus endured great hostility from sinners.
Think about Jesus and what He suffered.
He faced opposition from sinful people.
Remember His endurance.
If you remember Him, you will not grow weary.
If you remember Him, you will not lose heart.
passages.original: ἀναλογίσασθε γὰρ τὸν τοιαύτην ὑπομεμενηκότα ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν εἰς ἑαυτὸν ἀντιλογίαν ἵνα μὴ κάμητε ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν ἐκλυόμενοι

passages.text: In your struggle against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.
passages.sermon: You are struggling against sin.\r\nYou have not resisted sin to the point of shedding your blood.
passages.original: Οὔπω μέχρις αἵματος ἀντικατέστητε πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνταγωνιζόμενοι

passages.text: And you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord, and do not lose heart when He rebukes you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to you as His sons.
He gives you an exhortation.
You have forgotten this exhortation.
God says, “My son, do not take lightly the Lord’s discipline.
Do not lose heart when the Lord rebukes you.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐκλέλησθε τῆς παρακλήσεως ἥτις ὑμῖν ὡς υἱοῖς διαλέγεται Υἱέ μου μὴ ὀλιγώρει παιδείας Κυρίου μηδὲ ἐκλύου ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐλεγχόμενος

passages.text: For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He chastises every son He receives.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord loves certain people.
The Lord disciplines those people.
The Lord receives some people as sons.
The Lord chastises every son He receives.
passages.original: ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ Κύριος παιδεύει μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται

passages.text: Endure suffering as discipline; God is treating you as sons. For what son is not disciplined by his father?
passages.sermon:
God is your Father.
God treats you as His sons.
You must endure suffering as discipline.
A father always disciplines his son.
No true son is without discipline from his father.
passages.original: Εἰς παιδείαν ὑπομένετε ὡς υἱοῖς ὑμῖν προσφέρεται ὁ Θεός τίς γὰρ υἱὸς ὃν οὐ παιδεύει πατήρ

passages.text: If you do not experience discipline like everyone else, then you are illegitimate children and not true sons.
passages.sermon:
God disciplines every true son.
All true sons share in discipline.
If you do not receive discipline,
You are not a true son.
You are an illegitimate child.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ χωρίς ἐστε παιδείας ἧς μέτοχοι γεγόνασιν πάντες ἄρα νόθοι καὶ οὐχ υἱοί ἐστε

passages.text: Furthermore, we have all had earthly fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Should we not much more submit to the Father of our spirits and live?
passages.sermon:
We all have earthly fathers.
Our earthly fathers disciplined us.
We respected our earthly fathers for this.
God is the Father of our spirits.
We should submit even more to God.
If we submit to God, we will live.
passages.original: εἶτα τοὺς μὲν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν πατέρας εἴχομεν παιδευτὰς καὶ ἐνετρεπόμεθα οὐ πολὺ δὲ μᾶλλον ὑποταγησόμεθα τῷ Πατρὶ τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ ζήσομεν

passages.text: Our fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our good, so that we may share in His holiness.
passages.sermon:
Earthly fathers disciplined us.
They did this for a short time.
They disciplined us as they thought best.
God disciplines us for our good.
God wants us to share in His holiness.
passages.original: Οἱ μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ὀλίγας ἡμέρας κατὰ τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς ἐπαίδευον ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ συμφέρον εἰς τὸ μεταλαβεῖν τῆς ἁγιότητος αὐτοῦ

passages.text: No discipline seems enjoyable at the time, but painful. Later on, however, it yields a harvest of righteousness and peace to those who have been trained by it.
passages.sermon:
Discipline does not seem joyful at the moment.
Discipline feels painful at the time.
Later, discipline produces a peaceful result.
Discipline gives righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
Discipline brings peace to those who accept its training.
passages.original: πᾶσα δὲ παιδεία πρὸς μὲν τὸ παρὸν οὐ δοκεῖ χαρᾶς εἶναι ἀλλὰ λύπης ὕστερον δὲ καρπὸν εἰρηνικὸν τοῖς δι’ αὐτῆς γεγυμνασμένοις ἀποδίδωσιν δικαιοσύνης

passages.text: Therefore strengthen your limp hands and weak knees.
passages.sermon:
God disciplines us for our good.
He wants us to share in His holiness.
Discipline can feel painful now.
Later, it produces righteousness and peace for those trained by it.
Therefore, strengthen your weak hands.
Strengthen your feeble knees.
passages.original: Διὸ τὰς παρειμένας χεῖρας καὶ τὰ παραλελυμένα γόνατα ἀνορθώσατε

passages.text: Make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame may not be disabled, but rather healed.
passages.sermon:
You must make straight paths for your feet.
This means you should choose a clear and right way to walk.
If you do this, those who are lame will not be led astray.
Instead, the lame will be healed.
passages.original: καὶ τροχιὰς ὀρθὰς ποιεῖτε τοῖς ποσὶν ὑμῶν ἵνα μὴ τὸ χωλὸν ἐκτραπῇ ἰαθῇ δὲ μᾶλλον

passages.text: Pursue peace with everyone, as well as holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
passages.sermon:
This instruction comes from the letter to the Hebrews in the New Testament.
The writer addresses Christians.
He urges them to pursue peace with everyone.
He also urges them to pursue holiness.
No one will see the Lord without holiness.
passages.original: Εἰρήνην διώκετε μετὰ πάντων καὶ τὸν ἁγιασμόν οὗ χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν Κύριον

passages.text: See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God, and that no root of bitterness springs up to cause trouble and defile many.
passages.sermon:
God gives grace to people.
This grace is a gift from God.
You must watch over each other.
Make sure no one misses out on God’s grace.
A root of bitterness can grow among people.
This bitterness causes trouble.
Bitterness can spread to many people.
Bitterness can make many people unclean.
passages.original: ἐπισκοποῦντες μή τις ὑστερῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Θεοῦ μή τις ῥίζα πικρίας ἄνω φύουσα ἐνοχλῇ καὶ δι’ αὐτῆς μιανθῶσιν οἱ πολλοί

passages.text: See to it that no one is sexually immoral, or is godless like Esau, who for a single meal sold his birthright.
passages.sermon: See to it that no one is sexually immoral.\r\nSee to it that no one is godless like Esau.\r\nEsau sold his birthright for a single meal.
passages.original: μή τις πόρνος ἢ βέβηλος ὡς Ἠσαῦ ὃς ἀντὶ βρώσεως μιᾶς ἀπέδετο τὰ πρωτοτόκια ἑαυτοῦ

passages.text: For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. He could find no ground for repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears.
passages.sermon:
Esau was a man who sold his birthright for a single meal.
Later, Esau wanted to receive the blessing from God.
He tried to inherit this blessing.
But Esau was rejected.
He could not find a way to repent.
He looked for the blessing with tears.
But he did not receive it.
passages.original: ἴστε γὰρ ὅτι καὶ μετέπειτα θέλων κληρονομῆσαι τὴν εὐλογίαν ἀπεδοκιμάσθη μετανοίας γὰρ τόπον οὐχ εὗρεν καίπερ μετὰ δακρύων ἐκζητήσας αὐτήν

passages.text: For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire; to darkness, gloom, and storm; to a trumpet blast or to a voice that made its hearers beg that no further word be spoken.
passages.sermon:
You have not come to a mountain that people can touch.
This mountain burned with fire.
It was covered in darkness.
It was filled with gloom.
A storm surrounded it.
A trumpet sounded there.
A voice spoke words from the mountain.
The people who heard the voice begged for no more words to be spoken to them.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ προσεληλύθατε ψηλαφωμένῳ καὶ κεκαυμένῳ πυρὶ καὶ γνόφῳ καὶ ζόφῳ καὶ θυέλλῃ καὶ σάλπιγγος ἤχῳ καὶ φωνῇ ῥημάτων ἧς οἱ ἀκούσαντες παρῃτήσαντο μὴ προστεθῆναι αὐτοῖς λόγον

passages.text: For they could not bear what was commanded: “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”
passages.sermon: God gave a command at Mount Sinai.\r\nThe people could not bear this command.\r\nThe command said, “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”
passages.original: οὐκ ἔφερον γὰρ τὸ διαστελλόμενον Κἂν θηρίον θίγῃ τοῦ ὄρους λιθοβοληθήσεται

passages.text: The sight was so terrifying that even Moses said, “I am trembling with fear.”
passages.sermon:
God appeared on Mount Sinai.
God showed His power with fire, darkness, and storm.
The people saw this display.
The sight was terrifying.
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Even Moses saw the sight.
Moses said, “I am trembling with fear.”
passages.original: καί οὕτω φοβερὸν ἦν τὸ φανταζόμενον Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν Ἔκφοβός εἰμι καὶ ἔντρομος

passages.text: Instead, you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have come to myriads of angels in joyful assembly, to the congregation of the firstborn, enrolled in heaven. You have come to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous made perfect, to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
passages.sermon:
You have come to Mount Zion.
Mount Zion is the city of the living God.
This city is the heavenly Jerusalem.
You have come to countless angels.
These angels gather in joyful assembly.
You have come to the congregation of the firstborn.
The firstborn are enrolled in heaven.
You have come to God.
God is the Judge of all.
You have come to the spirits of righteous people.
These righteous people have been made perfect.
You have come to Jesus.
Jesus is the mediator of a new covenant.
You have come to sprinkled blood.
This blood speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ προσεληλύθατε Σιὼν ὄρει καὶ πόλει Θεοῦ ζῶντος Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ καὶ μυριάσιν ἀγγέλων πανηγύρει καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς καὶ Κριτῇ Θεῷ πάντων καὶ πνεύμασι δικαίων τετελειωμένων καὶ διαθήκης νέας μεσίτῃ Ἰησοῦ καὶ αἵματι ῥαντισμοῦ κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι παρὰ τὸν Ἅβελ

passages.text: See to it that you do not refuse Him who speaks. For if the people did not escape when they refused Him who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we reject Him who warns us from heaven?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to us.
Do not refuse Him.
Long ago, God warned people on earth.
Those people did not escape when they refused Him.
Now, God warns us from heaven.
If we reject Him, we will not escape.
passages.original: Βλέπετε μὴ παραιτήσησθε τὸν λαλοῦντα εἰ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι οὐκ ἐξέφυγον ἐπὶ γῆς παραιτησάμενοι τὸν χρηματίζοντα πολὺ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς οἱ τὸν ἀπ’ οὐρανῶν ἀποστρεφόμενοι

passages.text: At that time His voice shook the earth, but now He has promised, “Once more I will shake not only the earth, but heaven as well.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke with a powerful voice in the past.
His voice shook the earth at that time.
Now God has made a promise.
He said, “Once more I will shake the earth.”
He also said, “I will shake heaven as well.”
passages.original: οὗ ἡ φωνὴ τὴν γῆν ἐσάλευσεν τότε νῦν δὲ ἐπήγγελται λέγων Ἔτι ἅπαξ ἐγὼ σείσω οὐ μόνον τὴν γῆν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν οὐρανόν

passages.text: The words “Once more” signify the removal of what can be shaken—that is, created things—so that the unshakable may remain.
passages.sermon:
God promised to shake the earth and heaven once more.
The words “Once more” mean God will remove things that can be shaken.
Created things can be shaken.
God will remove these created things.
Unshakable things will remain.
passages.original: τὸ δὲ Ἔτι ἅπαξ δηλοῖ τὴν τῶν σαλευομένων μετάθεσιν ὡς πεποιημένων ἵνα μείνῃ τὰ μὴ σαλευόμενα

passages.text: Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us be filled with gratitude, and so worship God acceptably with reverence and awe.
passages.sermon:
We are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
This kingdom is unshakable.
Let us be thankful.
Let us worship God in a way that pleases Him.
Let us worship with reverence.
Let us worship with awe.
passages.original: Διὸ βασιλείαν ἀσάλευτον παραλαμβάνοντες ἔχωμεν χάριν δι’ ἧς λατρεύωμεν εὐαρέστως τῷ Θεῷ μετὰ εὐλαβείας καὶ δέους

passages.text: “For our God is a consuming fire.”
passages.sermon: God is our God.\r\nGod is a consuming fire.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον
